packages.label: גְּבוּרָה וְחֹזֶק הַלֵּב
packages.reason: The Rebbe establishes that גְּבוּרָה (bravery/heroism) and חֹזֶק הַלֵּב (strength of the heart) share the same essential nature — they are two faces of the same reality. He states explicitly: 'עִקָּר הַגְּבוּרָה הוּא בַּלֵּב' — the essence of bravery IS in the heart. This is a bechina statement equating the two. The גִּבּוֹר (the hero/warrior) is defined by this same quality — he is not a separate cause of bravery but is the bechina of the one who possesses חֹזֶק לֵב. The concepts of אֹמֶץ לֵב (courage of heart) and חֹזֶק לֵב are used interchangeably in the same clause ('חֹזֶק וְאֹמֶץ לִבּוֹ'), making them bechina-identical expressions of the same inner quality. These concepts all describe the same positive spiritual-psychological reality: the domain of inner heroism rooted in the heart.

packages.label: חֲלִישׁוּת הַלֵּב וְהַיִּרְאָה
packages.reason: The Rebbe establishes the evil mirror of Package 1: חֲלִישׁוּת הַלֵּב (weakness of the heart) is the essential nature of the domain of fear. Rashi's gloss — cited explicitly by the Rebbe — equates 'הַיָּרֵא' (the fearful one) with 'רַךְ הַלֵּבָב' (soft-heartedness), making these bechina-identical: to be fearful IS to have a soft heart; to have a soft heart IS to be fearful. The Rebbe confirms this equation: 'כִּי עַל־יְדֵי רַךְ־לֵבָב... הוּא מִתְיָרֵא, כַּנַּ"ל'. The 'כַּנַּ"ל' (as above) is a classic bechina marker — the Rebbe is saying rakh-levav IS the same as the previous description of fear. פַּחַד (fear/terror) and יִרְאָה (timidity/fear) are two names for the same experienced reality that flows from this weak-hearted nature. This is the evil/negative polarity counterpart to Package 1: where Package 1 has חֹזֶק לֵב, Package 2 has חֲלִישׁוּת הַלֵּב; where Package 1 has the גִּבּוֹר, Package 2 has the יָרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב.
